decision.reason: River and stream environments require intrinsic directional current, longitudinal channel travel, cross-current crossing, bank access/egress, ford/choke-point behavior, and channel obstacles. Open Water Surface lacks stable bank/channel semantics and Wetland lacks directional channel flow, so composing only the ENV-03 archetypes would either lose reusable behavior or duplicate it across freshwater presets.

archetypes.name: Flowing Water / Channel
archetypes.baseline_scope: Channelized surface water where directional flow, a defined bed and banks, longitudinal travel, cross-current movement, access/egress points, and channel obstacles shape navigation and exposure.
reusable_behavior: rapids shallows debris bars and other channel obstacles
ordinary water-level variability without assuming an active flood disaster
evidence_basis: ENV-03 explicit flowing-water/channel gap watch item

non_promotions.reason: Lake/Pond does not require a new structural archetype; freshwater chemistry and scale are preset parameters while Open Water Surface already owns surface-water traversal.
The meaningful differences are hydrology/substrate/nutrient/vegetation parameterization within Wetland rather than new universal topology.
Persistent or ordinary waterlogged forest structure is a compound baseline; exceptional active flooding remains a later hydrology overlay.
The river-mouth interface is compound; ENV-07 retains detailed coastal/tidal/marine refinement.
